# Rename Contract Checklist: Rename Symphony to Symphony Plus

**Purpose**: Lightweight peer-review gate for the completeness and consistency of the full product rename requirements
**Created**: 2026-10-13
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are canonical values specified for product prose, commands, paths, labels, branch names, release artifacts, Elixir identities, environment variables, and persisted names? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001–FR-008]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the normative specification, operator guides, workflow examples, templates, and release documentation all included in the rename scope? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK003 Are targeted regression coverage and the full quality gate both explicitly required for the renamed interfaces? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, §SC-004]

## Requirement Clarity and Consistency

- [ ] CHK004 Is the display-name versus machine-slug mapping unambiguous and consistent across requirements and the naming contract? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001–FR-008]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the no-alias breaking-change policy consistent for executables, commands, labels, workflow directories, and persisted paths? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK006 Are intentional upstream and immutable-external exceptions narrowly classified without permitting unexplained legacy branding? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, Edge Cases]

## Acceptance and Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK007 Can every measurable outcome be traced to an operator, documentation, audit, or regression-validation scenario? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–SC-005]
- [ ] CHK008 Are fresh-install, removed-legacy-interface, and retained-upstream-reference scenarios all addressed by acceptance criteria? [Coverage, Spec §User Stories 1–3]
- [ ] CHK009 Are startup, reload, restart, dispatch, retry, reconciliation, cancellation, cleanup, review, and merge-queue preservation requirements explicit where renamed identities participate? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013]

## Dependencies and Edge Cases

- [ ] CHK010 Is workflow-safe sequencing for the live GitHub label rename defined clearly enough to avoid interrupting the active durable workflow? [Dependency, Spec §FR-005, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK011 Are collision behavior and the absence of automatic migration or fallback for legacy persisted paths stated consistently? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases; Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK012 Are workspace, credential, secret-handling, and repository-boundary invariants explicitly preserved during all path and identity renames? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
